Subject: Private GPU pool: provisioning & network acceptance tests

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Thanks for the runbook review last week. We're ready to move from design -> acceptance for the private VPC deployment Redwood will manage for Orion. Before we kick off the acceptance window we need a clear, agreed plan for capacity and the network acceptance tests. High level asks: 

- Sustained target: 30 qps (combined text generations) with 95th latency < 250ms as the operational SLO.
- Burst target: handle 300 qps peaks for up to 5 minutes without dropping below a 99% success rate.
- Egress: our VPC uplink is currently quoted at 10 Gbps; need per-GPU egress estimates and admission-control plan if we hit NIC limits.
- NAT scaling: we use per-subnet NAT gateways; please confirm SNAT capacity and any port exhaustion mitigations.

What we'd like from Redwood before acceptance: a single-page mutual action plan with the following sections: capacity matrix (nodes, GPU type, expected sustained qps per GPU), scaling triggers (metrics + thresholds), network acceptance checklist (MTU, TCP tuning, NIC settings, firewall rules), and a proposed 3-hour acceptance test window.

Can you share the capacity matrix draft and a proposed test window by EOD Friday PST? Procurement has also asked for an estimated monthly committed throughput so they can prep a PO (cc'd).

Thanks,
Ellen

Ellen — thanks, this is clear and actionable. Draft action plan below and attached is a first-pass capacity_matrix_v1.csv (stub). Attachment: capacity_matrix_v1.csv (CSV, 24KB).

Proposed mutual action plan (summary)
- Baseline cluster: 6 x A100-80GB (reserved) giving ~6k tokens/s aggregate for our model mix; expected sustained throughput ~32 qps for your workload profile.
- Burst capacity: scale pool to 18 nodes via burst autoscale (policy: CPU+queue depth) to cover short 300 qps windows. Warm pool of 4 standby nodes to reduce cold-start KV-cache penalty.
- Per-GPU assumptions: conservative per-GPU sustained serving capacity = 5 qps (95th latency target), peak transient = 25 qps during warm cache window.
- Admission control: token-based admission with a sliding window; when token pool falls below 20% we shed low-priority requests and route to fallback smaller model.
- Network: assume 25% headroom on 10 Gbps egress for other customer traffic; plan for NIC oversubscription guardrail and prioritize control plane and KV warmup traffic.

Network acceptance checklist (high level)
- MTU >= 9000 on private fabric; validate jumbo frames across host switches.
- Verify SR-IOV enabled on GPU hosts (if using parasitic NICs) and that SR-IOV VF count >= expected concurrency.
- TCP window tuning: initial 64MB window recommendation for high-latency cross-region links (we'll tailor if you're fully in-region).
- NAT gateway scale plan: we'll supply ephemeral port usage estimates per host; recommend a pool of 3 NAT gateways per subnet for failure/fanout.

Proposed acceptance window
- Prefer Fri 24 Mar 2028 02:00-05:00 PDT (3 hours) — test includes ramp to sustained load, 2x burst simulation, and failover/rollback check.

Next steps: Laura, Jonas — can you review the CSV and network checklist? Ellen — if the timing works, we'll lock the window and publish a runbook link.

- Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer

Thanks Karthik — good draft. A few operational items to add to the network acceptance checklist and the acceptance runbook:

Network acceptance additions (ops)
- Validate NIC firmware & driver versions across hosts; mismatches can cause packet drops under load.
- Verify host-level eBPF offloads and ensure packet drops are not hidden by offload.
- Confirm firewall rules allow health-checks + control-plane ports from Redwood control IPs (we'll provide CIDRs).
- Congestion control: enable fq_codel on worker NICs to avoid bufferbloat during large KV cache repop.

Runbook / handoff
- On-call: Redwood will handoff to Orion SRE with a single-point escalation list (primary + backfill).
- Rollback criteria: >1% 5xxs sustained for 2 minutes OR 95th latency > 500ms for 5 minutes.
- Preflight checks (30 min): cache prefill progress, node health, NIC counters.

Jonas / Marissa — please confirm the autoscale trigger thresholds and the telemetry dashboards we'll put on the console.

Laura
Head of Product Ops

Ellen / team — locking acceptance window and publishing the short checklist. Thanks for the diagram and PO confirmation.

Acceptance test window: Tue 28 Mar 2028 14:00-17:00 PDT (we will start 30m earlier for preflight and end 30m for teardown).

Checklist (abbreviated)
1) Preflight (T-30m)
   - Node health & firmware verified
   - MTU / jumbo frames validated across switches
   - NAT gateway port availability check (we'll run a port-consumption probe)
   - KV cache prefill started and progress visible in metrics (console link below)
2) Ramp to sustained (T+0 to T+45m)
   - Target sustained 30 qps; monitor 95th latency < 250ms
   - Validate ingress/egress counters; abort if egress > 9Gbps sustained
3) Burst tests (T+45 to T+90m)
   - Simulate 300 qps spikes in two 2-min bursts; validate no >1% 5xx
4) Failover & rollback (T+90 to T+120m)
   - Force single-node failure; validate warm-pool absorption and autoscale to target nodes
   - If rollback criteria met (see Laura's note), enact rollback plan

Attachments for runbook: capacity_matrix_v1.csv, network-diagram.pdf. Preflight runbook hosted: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCExampleSharedRunbook
JIRA ticket for tracking: ORION-4572
